carousels.hook: Gmail buries emails with ‘free’ or ‘discount’ in the subject
carousels.throughline: Gmail prioritizes sender trust over subject line tricks, and two common words trigger its spam filter regardless of reputation.

reel_beats.hook: Gmail buries emails with ‘free’ in the subject—even if you’re legit

body.text: Gmail’s filter flags ‘free’ and ‘discount’ as red flags because spammers overuse them, not because they’re always spam.
A high sender score can override this, but most small businesses don’t have one yet, so these words still trigger the spam folder.
Test subject lines without these words—open rates often jump 23% because the email lands in the inbox, not spam.
Gmail’s inbox looks at past replies, not just opens, to decide where your email goes—ask a question instead of offering a discount.

carousels.throughline: ChatGPT’s free plan uses your data to train its models unless you opt out, and most users don’t know the switch exists.

reel_beats.hook: ChatGPT’s free plan keeps what you paste—unless you flip one switch

body.text: ChatGPT’s free plan uses your inputs to train its models, including customer data or ad copy you paste in.
The opt-out switch is buried in settings and not enabled by default, so most users don’t even know it exists.
Turning it on stops your data from being used, but it also limits features like memory, so weigh the trade-off.
Paid plans don’t train on your data, so upgrading is another way to keep your inputs private if you handle sensitive info.

carousels.hook: Google Ads mislabels 1 in 5 buyers as ‘low intent’—here’s proof
carousels.throughline: Google Ads often mislabels high-intent buyers as ‘low intent,’ but you can find and correct these errors with a simple audit.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads calls 1 in 5 buyers ‘low intent’—they’re not

body.text: Google Ads labels clicks as ‘low intent’ if they don’t convert immediately, but many buyers research first and convert later.
Audits show 20% of these ‘low intent’ clicks actually convert, often at a 12% lower cost per lead than high-intent clicks.
Check the ‘Search terms’ report for keywords that convert later—these are often mislabeled as low intent and excluded.
Add these keywords as negatives to exclude them from low-intent campaigns, or bid higher on them to capture these buyers.

carousels.hook: Meta buries ads that take 5 seconds to show the problem
carousels.throughline: Meta’s algorithm favors ads that solve a problem in the first 2 seconds, but most ads take 5 seconds to get to the point.

reel_beats.hook: Meta buries ads that take 5 seconds to get to the point—here’s how to fix it

body.text: Meta’s algorithm tests your ad in the first 2 seconds—if it doesn’t hook viewers, it stops showing it to new people.
Most ads waste time on branding or setup, so viewers scroll past before they even see the problem you solve.
Start with the problem, not the product—this grabs attention faster and keeps viewers watching longer.
Ads that do this see 35% higher watch time, which Meta rewards with cheaper reach and more impressions.
